question: Metformin should be withheld in patients with CKD when eGFR falls below 30 mL/min/1.73 m² due to the risk of lactic acidosis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The metformin safety threshold is eGFR 30 mL/min/1.73 m². Below this, metformin accumulates and lactic acidosis risk is unacceptable. Between eGFR 30–45, use with caution; below 30, withhold.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Metformin is contraindicated (hold/stop) when eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (G4–G5) because reduced renal clearance of metformin causes accumulation and risk of life-threatening lactic acidosis. At eGFR 30–45 (G3b), metformin may be continued with caution and dose review. At eGFR <30, stop it.
